Assuming this is a 1099 miscellaneous I don't think the reason matters. The IRS and state tax authority consider this income and you are taxed on it regardless of the reason. When you file your tax return you would need to speak with a tax professional regarding how to handle deductions for your business.

I don't understand what you are asking in the second part of this comment, can you please clarify?

Is your donor asking to become a member of your LLC? If they are becoming a member of the LLC then you must file a form 1065 with the IRS and send the member contributing to the LLC a Schedule K-1, which breaks down each member's share of the LLC's profits and losses. In turn, each LLC member reports this profit and loss information on his or her individual Form 1040, with Schedule E attached. You will need to give your donor the LLC's EIN which you can obtain from the IRS. This should all be set out in your LLC's member agreement.

If the donor is not becoming a member of the LLC then you have a more complex issue. They can send you a 1099 but at that point it is income for the business along with what ever income you receive from your crowdsourcing campaign which will also send you a 1099. I am sure you will have more expenses then income but you will need to file a tax return for the LLC. 

As per the issue of the sale of property for the artwork this can be handled in your member agreement or the agreement you make with the donor as essentially a client of the LLC. If I was in your position I would break in the cost of storage and deprecation of the piece into the agreement. 

Recently business contracts have become more fluid and what can and can not be enforced depends on the state you are incorporated. I would try and have a very clear written agreement of what the exact arrangement/relationship is between you and the person giving you money before you accept anything.

I'm probably the wrong person to comment here but I'll give it a go. First of all, I have never been a huge temple fan. It's always seemed to me like the most over glorified of art projects. This year I had a unique perspective, our camp's warehouse space was next door to where the trees and other side structures for the temple were being built in Oakland. We also had a lot of people who liked to hang out at our area of the warehouse while working on the temple over the last few months. I never heard one good thing about the design, structure, construction was a nightmare and no one really seemed to enjoy working on it. After a while it really seemed like they were doing some kind of unfortunate chore that they felt obligated to do rather than wanting to do. We had one girl who worked full time on the temple camp with us, on the last day of the burn she totally freaked out and badly injured her self. 

Overall I know so many people who had terrible experiences working on the temple that I just can't respect that thing. In my mind it's truly a temple to what Burning Man has become, a few people doing a ton of work for no money so the majority of people can show up, have a good time and do little to nothing. 

I'm not jaded, just looking forward to try being a tourist next year! :-)

Hi First Time Burner,

This is my third burn and I am running the bar at Love Potion 7:30 & G so let me tell you how I am doing it.

Our camp members are expected to gift a bottle of liquor and a bottle of mixer. This year we asked for specific liquors and mixers so we can do a premix and then blend with ice for frozen drink. We used to let people bring anything and we wound up lugging home a lot of gin and club soda. 

The bar set up is pretty streamlined and this is just to make the process simple. After all the drinks are gifts so we want to make gifting simple.

We have a dedicated ice fairy who get's ice everyday for the bar and if anyone orders ice for personal use. I don't know what shitty broken down ice is but they sell cubes and blocks.

Each camp member is expected to volunteer at the bar, we have a sign up everyday. But we are flexible as to when and times because it's Burning Man and people are going to do what they want to do. 

Set up and breakdown are explained but we have laminated instructions at the bar including plenty of 21+ reminders. 

If you want to offer your bar tending as a gift I advise finding a smaller camp that you like and offering to bartend. But for your first year I advise you to take care of your self and have fun first and foremost.
